Please think twice before registering your beloved pet with this veterinary clinic. While the staff initially come across as polite, helpful, and welcoming, it is a false front. Once you are locked in, their true colors emerge.This clinic operates with a deeply troubling, money-driven culture that prioritizes profit over the actual welfare of animals. Based on my experience, this is not an isolated incident at one location; the entire network of branches seems to share the exact same toxic culture. This company has even been under formal investigation for wrongdoing in the past.My primary grievances include:Discriminatory Attitude: The customer service is incredibly poor, and staff exhibit a biased and discriminatory attitude toward clients.Blind Prescribing: They repeatedly dispense expensive medications without conducting proper diagnostics first. They rely on assumptions rather than medical tests.Imposed & Expensive Costs: They force costly treatments and medications onto pets that do not even need them, racking up massive bills.Delayed Diagnosis: Because they prefer guessing over proper testing, they take far too long to diagnose an animal's true sickness.Tragic Outcomes: By the time they finally realize the true issue, it is too late. They then pressure you to put your animal down—a heartbreaking situation that could have been avoided with competent, early care.They are running a business, not a medical practice that cares for animals. Save your pet’s life and your own sanity by taking your business to an independent, caring veterinarian instead.

My 2-year-old cat died after being mistreated at this clinic, and I cannot describe the level of disappointment and frustration we experienced.

We brought him in multiple times over the course of a week, four visits in total. After the first visit, where a fever was identified, there was a shocking lack of proper follow-up. Basic checks were not consistently performed, and no one seemed to be closely monitoring his condition.

By the second visit, he was already showing clear signs of jaundice and anaemia, serious and alarming symptoms. Yet we were simply told to continue medication and come back later. No urgency. No thorough investigation. No escalation.

By the third visit, he had barely eaten for nearly a week. We were extremely worried, but instead of taking decisive action, we were repeatedly told to “wait and observe” and were given only appetite stimulants. We had to beg for hospitalisation and IV fluids ourselves.

What is most upsetting is that no one ever told us how critical his condition actually was. At no point were we advised to seek emergency care or go to a better-equipped hospital. We trusted the professionals, but that trust was completely misplaced.

Every visit was handled by a different vet. There was no continuity, no clear responsibility, and no sense that anyone truly understood how serious his condition had become.

This was not just miscommunication. This was a failure to recognise and act on a deteriorating, life-threatening condition.

Our cat might still be here if proper care and urgency had been given.

Instead, we lost him.

I would not wish this experience on anyone.

Heartbroken 😭😭. Just had to say goodbye to our big dopey teddy bear of a dog at the emergency Willow vets in Solihull 😭😭💔.  Pype Hayes vets are bloody disgusting!!!! Last 3 weeks we've been taking him there after him having a bland diet of boiled chicken for 5 days didn't sort his bad tummy (constant diarrhea with mucus) and not getting better.
First week they gave antibiotics, (his temp was a bit high), they didn't work.
2nd week took him back..they gave omeprazole antacids and a stool sample bottle incase they didn't work. They didn't!...
Took stool sample in last Wednesday (£229.15!! And not heard anything back as of this posting).
2 days later on the Friday morning at 10.30 am I rung them and said we need to book him for a scan as he's deteriorating badly, i was really worried. He was looking quite thin at this stage, drooling and panting, hackles all up along back indicating he was in pain and still having very bad diarrhea. I was really worried.  Stool test wasn't back..I was told to take him in before 11 they said if I thought it was urgent. It wasn't possible as husband works 2 hours away and i don't drive so asked if he could be booked in for a scan (he's a very big dog and taxis don't like taking dogs full stop).
They don't book for scans they said, but bring him in for a full health check on the evening and if needs be will direct to out of hours for a scan..
Friday evening appointment they checked heart and temp ( temp still a bit high again they said... but she said probably from being in the car and waiting room) and just gave painkillers and MORE ANTACIDS 😡.
Next day..late Saturday night he was restless, didn't want to lie down. Drooling even more but eventually he went to sleep.
Sunday morning he started vomiting bright yellow bile. Had to rush him to the emergency Willow vets in Solihull. He collapsed when we got him out of the car and again in the waiting room.
They weighed him (he'd lost 4 kg's in 3 weeks)  and temperature of 42!! Dehydrated and critical😭😭😡😡.  They rushed him straight in for IV fluids and gave him a scan straight away. He'd got fluid round his heart!!!!
They drained the fluid (700 ml), managed to drop temp slightly to 40 but heart rate high 😭. Said he was critical, would do CT scan for imaging see what's going on. Had to pay 3k out of the 6k minimum quote before leaving him there. Said to keep phone near as touch and go. But i had a bit of hope when i hadn't had a call by midnight...our brave boy a strong fighter. He was only 4...strong young boy ..
Then the phone rings at 01.14.
He's in bad way. Vomiting blood and bloody diarrhea and blood pressure dropping😭😭.
Drove up there straight away...oh God, our poor boy 😭😭. Can see blood in his drainage bag,  he's not responsive, and nurse said he could likely deteriorate and go into cardiac arrest at any time 😭. So we had to do the right thing...no way were we leaving our boy on his own for that to happen. We had to make the call 💔💔💔😭😭😭.
Our sweet sweet dopey boy. Pype Hayes vets should be ashamed!!!!!😡😡😡😡.
After being with them for 30 years and lining their pockets with thousands of pounds we will NEVER EVER EVER take another pet of ours there!!! They just don't care anymore. It's just about the money since Medivet took over.!!

Update to my previous positive review.

This practice used to be really well rated, had an excellent reputation in the local area, and was regularly recommended by myself to others.

I'd heard bad things since it was taken over by Medivet but finally got to see it for myself a couple of months ago when my elderly cat needed to be put to sleep.

From the initial phone call we were made to feel like we were being a nuisance by calling up and asking for an emergency appointment for euthanasia. When we arrived we were kept waiting a long time at reception. We were not shown straight into a consultation room as has previously happened when I have taken a pet in to say goodbye, we were made to wait surrounded by other animals including barking dogs in the waiting area.

Pretty sure they used to have a candle they lit on the reception desk when someone was saying goodbye to their pet, just to let others know to be respectful, this would have cost literal pennies - but this has apparently been sacrificed on the altar of the bottom line. They also had chocolates for dogs who were passing, these have gone too.
